title: The Thicket That Learned Its Own Sermon

features.name: the-sermon-vines
features.desc-on-touch: words grow through the thicket like sentences turned into tendrils, each prayer-phrase catching light as it tangles deeper

features.name: the-reciting-stone
features.desc-on-touch: a low stone half-buried in the dusk, its surface covered in text that shifts from prayer to plant-matter as you read

features.name: the-knot-of-refusals
features.desc-on-touch: branches twisted into the shape of a throat mid-sermon, where the prayer refused to continue and the thicket took over the speaking

features.name: the-margin-where-words-root
features.desc-on-touch: at the edge of the thicket, you see language learning to root, syllables putting down tendrils into the soil

features.name: the-silence-that-grew
features.desc-on-touch: a pocket in the thicket where every prayer-phrase has become still, where speaking learned to wait

inscription: the thicket learned to pray and then forgot which was the prayer

file.name: Sermon_Midwinter_Abandoned_1987.txt
file.note: a sermon halted mid-breath, the pages corrupted so each line branches into prayer-vine, the speaker's voice left inside the leaves

reverie.title: REVERIE — a sanctuary of dusk and falling words
narr: you kneel beside her on the worn carpet, the autumn
light through the high windows turning words into
something you can hold without speaking. her hand
stays on your shoulder. above you, the rafters
full of small echoes, each one a prayer nobody
finished saying. the silence between you both grows

exits.label: back where the mutation spreads like grammar
into the clearing where the thicket refuses to grow
deeper thickets where other sermons learned to root
toward understory-floor where prayer-vines tangle into soil
